deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is the continuation and close of Riemann's formal Latin petition to the Göttingen Philosophical Faculty for the doctoral degree. The petition begins on the previous page: 'Ab amplissimo philosophorum ordine ... doctoris gradum petit G. F. B. Riemann Breselenzius, stud. math.'

The text on this page reads: '...sit exigua, philosophiae doctorem me creetis. Specimini dignitatis scripsi dissertationem, quae in jaciendis fundamentis theoriae generalis functionum complexae quantitatis variabilis versatur [replacing 'collocata est']. Quam Vobis jam subjicere judicibus audeo. Scripsi Gottingae [inserted above the line] (die XXIX, apparently struck) mensis Octobris anni MDCCCLI. G. F. B. Riemann, stud. math.'

Translation, joined to the previous page: 'Having devoted myself to the study of mathematics and physics for five years, I now ask you, most venerable men, that on account of my knowledge of these arts, which I feel to be slight, you create me Doctor of Philosophy. As a specimen of worthiness I have written a dissertation which is concerned with laying the foundations of a general theory of functions of a variable complex quantity. I now venture to submit it to you as judges. Written at Göttingen, (29th day) of the month of October, 1851.'

The dissertation referred to is Riemann's Inauguraldissertation 'Grundlagen für eine allgemeine Theorie der Functionen einer veränderlichen complexen Grösse' (Göttingen 1851). Gauss refereed it, and Riemann defended it in December 1851. The faint mirrored lines visible lower on the page are bleed-through from the reverse side or a facing sheet, not text on this page.
errors: No mathematical content, so there are no mathematical errors.

The draft-like corrections appear to be in a lighter ink or pencil and possibly a different stroke weight: 'versatur' over the cancelled 'collocata est', and 'Gottingae' above the line. This suggests a later revision of the wording, perhaps to adjust phrasing or leave the exact submission date open.

results.what: Formal Latin petition (Gesuch) for admission to the doctorate, naming the dissertation on the foundations of a general theory of functions of a complex variable, dated October 1851
results.modern_name: Doctoral petition accompanying Riemann's 1851 dissertation (Grundlagen für eine allgemeine Theorie der Functionen einer veränderlichen complexen Grösse)
results.usually_credited_to: Bernhard Riemann (1851); the dissertation is well known and published

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine administrative document: the closing of Riemann's well-known doctoral petition. Its only historical interest is documentary (the October 1851 dating and small wording revisions), and it contains no mathematics.

checkable.asserts: The Roman date MDCCCLI equals 1851, the year of Riemann's dissertation.
The (possibly cancelled) day 'XXIX' equals 29, i.e. 29 October 1851.

transcription_corrections: 'Gottingae' is written above the line (interlinear insertion) over 'die XXIX'. Whether 'die XXIX' is actually struck through or merely underlined is not fully certain from the image; the stroke looks like a cancellation, but this should be checked against the original.
'versatur' is an interlinear replacement written above 'collocata est', which is struck through; the transcription's markup is correct.
The faint mirrored text in the middle and lower parts of the page is bleed-through and should not be transcribed as part of this page.
